title: iyO
award: Awwwards Site of the Day, Apr 2 2026 (Honors, SOTD). Credits: Enrico Deiana, Federico, Matteo Donini.
industry: Consumer hardware e-commerce: screenless 'audio computers' (iyO One, iyO yO, VAD Pro, Wand, Caps, App), Webflow + Shopify checkout.
signature: The home page is one fixed viewport where about 1.6 million GPU particles trace the nodal lines of a Chladni plate that re-tunes itself on random timers (modes m,n drawn from 3/5/7 every 6-12s, with per-frame vibration jitter), while a varying 40-80% share of the particles condenses into lowercase haiku and dissolves again, so a product about talking to computers is introduced as visible sound. The page never scrolls, and nothing waits for the visitor's input.

first_screen.composition: OBSERVED (desktop_00): full-bleed #101010 field of white particle grain arranged in concentric Chladni rings with a bright, text-block-shaped cloud in the centre: the particles are seeded on the haiku's letter positions at load (audit 2, bundle), so the first frame is text-shaped grain being released onto the nodal lines, not a glow. Floating dark capsule nav 375x62px centred at y=32 (iyO wordmark left, round 9-dot grid button, a double-bar divider, round cart bubble with count 0). Bottom-left at x=48: the only headline, 33.6px Magnetik in two lines, first part #DDDEE3 and the tail 'you can talk to' in a span at opacity .5 (.info__text-last{opacity:.5}), so the two tones are one colour at two opacities. Bottom-right: 'SHOP NOW' in 11.2px tracked mono beside a 64x78px rounded glass tile holding a product render. Nothing else: no hero button, no section below (document height 900).

layout.section_rhythm: Home has no sections: the plate re-tunes every 6-12s and the haiku condense and dissolve on a separate 7-13s loop, independent of input (the probe's 8 wheel steps only let time pass: one haiku holds in desktop_01-04, is gone in 05-06 and the next forms in 07). motion.smooth_scroll: Lenis 1.3.17 (unpkg lenis.css in the HTML; html class 'lenis'), verified config {infinite:false, lerp:0.125, smoothWheel:true, touchMultiplier:2, smoothTouch:false} driven by gsap.ticker. Correction (audit 2): the infinite:true block the first pass attributed to Lenis belongs to the product slider (virtual-scroll: infinite, snap, lerpFactor 0.3, dragSensitivity 0.005, snapStrength 0.1, speedDecay 0.85, mouseMultiplier 0.5, touchMultiplier 2). On home the document is 900px tall, so nothing scrolls and the wheel has no visible effect.
motion.preloader: None. The body fades from autoAlpha 0 to 1 once the app boots, and the particle layer fades in (visibility 0 -> 1 over 1s, 0.3s delay, power2.out) as soon as the 9 haiku JPGs have been sampled into position textures.
motion.intro_sequence: Verified (audit 2): at load every particle is seeded on a letter pixel of the last haiku texture (index min(10, count-1) = words9), so the field starts as a text-shaped cloud (desktop_00). The haiku loop then begins with texturePercent at 0, which releases those particles onto the Chladni lines, and condenses 40-80% of them back into the same haiku (desktop_01 blurry -> desktop_02 crisp). Each later cycle dissolves to 0, switches to the next texture, and condenses again (desktop_07 shows the next haiku forming).
scroll_techniques: none on home: the plate and haiku run on randomized gsap.delayedCall / tween loops, independent of scroll or wheel

plate modes: m and n drawn from [3,5,7] every 6-12s; patternFrequency 20-45 every 5-10s; patternJitter 0-0.3 every 4-8s; chladniNoise tweened to 0-0.5 over 2-5s power2.inOut; Chladni distortion tweened to 0-5 over 1.2-3s power2.inOut; each frame adds +/-0.45-0.52 random jitter to m and n before the shader rounds them, so the plate occasionally flickers to a neighbouring mode for a frame
haiku cycle: N = 3-6s; texturePercent -> 0 over 0.4N (dissolve), next texture, -> 0.4-0.8 over 0.6N (condense), hold 2-4s, -> new 0.4-0.8 over N/2, repeat
product pages: scroll-scrubbed character fill (SplitText chars autoAlpha 0.2 -> 1, stagger 0.1, scrub, start 'top 90%', end 'center 40%')
product pages: scroll-TRIGGERED (not scrubbed) exploded view, ScrollTrigger start 'top 50%', end 'bottom 50%', toggleActions 'play reverse play reverse'
motion.text_animation: Canvas haiku: particles are pulled to letter positions sampled from a word JPG, so text materialises from and dissolves into grain (desktop_01-04, element 0). DOM text, verified: GSAP SplitText {type:'words,chars', aria:'none'} blur-in: chars set to autoAlpha 0 + filter blur(2px), then autoAlpha 1 + blur(0) over 1.1s, ease linear, stagger each 0.02s from the start; triggered by an IntersectionObserver and reset to hidden when the element leaves, so it replays on every entry (element 3 f00 caught 'Say hel...' half-revealed). The h1 is one of these (34 char nodes). Product copy uses a separate scrubbed fill: SplitText {type:'words, chars', autoSplit:true} with autoAlpha 0.2 -> 1, stagger 0.1, ease linear, scrub from 'top 90%' to 'center 40%'. Reduced-motion users get the blur-in final state immediately.
motion.image_animation: Exploded view, verified (audit 2) against element 2 (3.48s clip): three GLB parts (outer disc, clear acoustic core, custom-fit tip) are offset along z by [0.6, 0.15, -0.6] x explodeProgress. A ScrollTrigger timeline (play at 'top 50%', reverse on leave) starts the group at ry = +pi/2, z 0.3, spins it to ry = -pi/2 and z 0 over 1s expo.inOut, and 0.5s into the spin runs explodeProgress 0 -> 1 over 1.8s with a CustomEase overshoot ('M0,0 C0,1.175 0.3,1.021 1,1'). That 180-degree spin is why f00-f07 go from 3/4 front to profile to rear (gold pogo pins) while the DETAILS label stays pinned at y=82 from f02 on. On top, the pointer tilts the group (rotation.x = mouseY*0.2, rotation.y = mouseX*0.2 rad) and an idle loop drifts y/rx/rz by a few hundredths over 3-5s sine.inOut. Hover (only once explodeProgress >= 0.4): the raycast part scales to 1.085-1.3 (disc 1.085, core 1.2, tip 1.2) and turns to a preset showcase angle while the other parts shrink to 0.8, all over 2.5s expo.out; a dark glass spec card (thumbnail, title, 3-4 line grey description: 'Audio computer disc', 'Acoustic system', 'Custom-fit tip') sits with its top-left at the pointer. Faint Chladni particles stay behind the model.
motion.page_transitions: Verified (audit 2): Taxi.js PJAX (data-taxi / data-taxi-view, links prefetched). Leave: [data-taxi] fades to autoAlpha 0 in 0.15s, body background switches to #DDDEE3 for /products or #101010 otherwise (so the swap never flashes the wrong colour), scroll resets to top. Enter: fade back to 1 over 0.2s after a 0.1s delay, then Shopyflow and Webflow IX are re-initialised. If the nav shell is missing it falls back to a hard navigation. The script also silences console.warn and console.error.
hover_micro: Part hover on the exploded model: hovered part grows to 1.085-1.3 and turns to a showcase angle, others shrink to 0.8 (2.5s expo.out), glass spec card at the pointer
SHOP NOW tile fans out into a vertical stack of 4 product thumbnails with the hovered product name in the label font (element 3 f06)
Configurator swatches: the product does NOT recolour instantly; a ripple wipe in UV space spreads the new matcap from the centre over 1.2s power2.out (see steal_this)

Nav capsule -> menu: the 23.5rem capsule's radius eases 3em -> 2em and its content row opens with grid-template-rows 0fr -> 1fr over 0.6s cubic-bezier(.625,.05,0,1); on close the radius waits 0.45s so it rounds only after the panel has folded; hovering a product card in the open menu dims the others to 0.2 and scales the hovered image to 1.04 (0.4s)
Footer video cards collapse to one card or expand to three depending on where the pointer is (element 3 f03 vs f06; trigger inferred)
motion.cursor: Home: native cursor (cursor:none 0); the pointer is a force in the particle sim (u_mouse, u_mouseVelocity). Configurator (verified audit 2, visible in element 1 f00/f01/f03/f06): a custom stage cursor is laid over the 3D viewport: a 3rem (48px) ring (.cursor_main) centred on the pointer plus a 0.45rem white ball (.cursor_ball) that trails on a second, slower follower, and side chevrons that slide out when the ring scales to 1.5 (0.5s expo.out) as a drag-to-rotate cue (horizontal chevrons only in image mode, both axes in 3D mode). It sits in a fixed, pointer-events:none layer, and the native arrow still shows alongside it.
easing_curves: app.css: cubic-bezier(.625,.05,0,1) x12, cubic-bezier(.48,.01,0,1.08) x11 (slight overshoot), cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) x7, cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) x3, cubic-bezier(.65,0,0,1) x3, cubic-bezier(.48,.01,0,1.15) x2, cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,.94) x2, cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1) x2, cubic-bezier(.5,.5,0,1) x1

GSAP string counts (audit 2 recount): power2.out x13, expo.out x11, none x7, power2.inOut x6, linear x5, back.out(0.8) x2, then single uses of expo.inOut, sine.inOut, power1.inOut, expo, power3, power4 and 'custom'
gsap.defaults({ease:'expo.out', duration:1.2}): every tween without its own ease is expo.out 1.2s
CustomEase 'custom' = M0,0 C0,1.175 0.3,1.021 1,1 (fast overshoot, used for the explode)
motion.duration_range_ms: CSS 100-800ms in the probe (mostly 250, 300, 200), app.css transitions 150-700ms (grid-rows 600-700ms); GSAP literals 150-2500ms, mostly 1000 (x8), 1200 (x7, and the global default), 800 (x7), 500 (x6); generative loops use random windows of 1.2-3s, 2-5s, 4-8s, 5-10s and 6-12s.
motion.choreography_notes: Element 0 (6.0s clip, frames at 0.37-5.61s): f00 haiku sits blurred inside a plus-shaped nodal outline; f01 (1.12s) a hollow ring has been punched through the middle column of letters while the cursor has already moved on to the upper right, so the disturbance outlives the pointer; f02 (1.87s) the plate mode flips to a square grid while the ring drifts right; f03 (2.62s) mode shifts to an H/plus figure, the third line smears into streaks where the cursor passed; f04-f05 (3.37-4.11s) letters spring back and re-sharpen; f06 (4.86s) crisp; f07 (5.61s) the haiku dims toward the next one. Four plate changes in 6s here are faster than the 6-12s mode timer, so the clip likely also catches frequency (5-10s) and distortion (1.2-3s) changes. Mechanism (verified): the pointer applies a RADIAL push only (home values: strength 0.0225, radius 0.16), scaled by a smoothed pointer speed (0.8/0.2 blend), so a still cursor does nothing; the hollow ring is what radial push plus friction leaves behind. Text particles are pulled back 5x harder than pattern particles (0.0025 vs 0.0005), velocity *= 0.985^(dt*60), so letters re-form in about 2.5-3s. u_patternSwirl (0.05) is a tangential shimmer ALONG the nodal lines, not a mouse swirl.

three_d.stack: three.js r178 (globals.three_revision) in a custom bundle hosted on iyo2.vercel.app and injected into Webflow; GLTFLoader + DRACOLoader + KTX2Loader + EXRLoader/RGBELoader, OrbitControls for the configurator, EffectComposer present in the bundle; hand-rolled GPGPU (two float render targets, no GPUComputationRenderer)
three_d.role: background field (GPGPU particles) on home + hero product (exploded view, configurator)
three_d.materials_lighting_post: Particles (verified audit 2): 1280x1280 float ping-pong targets = 1,638,400 particles drawn as 1px points (half-float fallback if float targets are unsupported). Word textures are NOT sampled in the sim shader: at load each JPG is drawn to a 400*dpr canvas, every dark pixel (red < 120) is collected, and each particle gets a random dark pixel as its text target in a float DataTexture (u_original). Sim fragment per particle: pickTexture = hash21(uv) < u_texturePercent (a stable random subset follows the text); target = mix(patternTarget, textTarget, pick); velocity *= pow(u_friction 0.985, dt*60); spring toward target (u_baseToShape 0.0005, x5 for text particles, pattern particles stop inside a 0.01 line-thickness band); random-direction noise (0.00035, x0.1 for text, x0.3 for pattern); radial mouse push within the radius, scaled by smoothed pointer speed (defaults 0.006 / 0.1, home overrides 0.0225 / 0.16); pos += velocity*dt*60; writes vec4(pos, velocity). Pattern targets come from computePatternPosition: a base pattern (8 presets) with nodal attraction 0.45, line push 0.12, a tangential shimmer along the lines (u_patternSwirl 0.05), frequency 35 (randomised 20-45), blended with a Chladni field sin(m*PI*x/a)*sin(n*PI*y/b), a=b=2, m and n rounded in-shader, plus one Newton step along the gradient (step = -field/|grad|, scaled 0.3*distortion). u_audioVolume / u_audioFrequency uniforms exist but stay 0. Product: MeshStandard/Physical presets from a table, e.g. glass {transmission 1, roughness 0.05, thickness 0.018, ior 1.6}, silicone tip {transmission 0.62, thickness 0.2, attenuationDistance 0.1, roughness 0.53, ior 1.42, #C7C7C7}, metals that swap colour per finish (changingDarkMetal variations #5A5A5A / #3F3F3F / #CDBEA7, changingLightMetal #868383 / #464646 / #FDF5EC; index-to-finish mapping inferred as Dusk / Night / Dawn); face colourways by an onBeforeCompile matcap patch over the PBR result (3 matcaps, uMatcapIntensity 0.82) lit by an EXR environment (hdr4.exr).
three_d.interaction: Pointer is a speed-scaled radial force in the particle sim; the plate re-tunes and the haiku cycle on timers (not on wheel); the exploded product spins on a scroll trigger, tilts with the pointer and responds to part hover; the configurator uses OrbitControls drag-to-rotate with a custom ring cursor, ripple-wipes matcaps per swatch and switches products.
three_d.performance_tactics: Two webgl2 contexts plus nine 2D canvases (probe contexts); the home canvas is 1440x900. 1.6M particles cost one full-screen sim pass per frame (no CPU physics), drawn as 1px points; pointer updates throttled to 16ms; text targets pre-sampled once on the CPU; whole 3D payload ~1MB (single GLB + EXR); colourways as matcap images rather than extra PBR maps; haiku as small JPGs.
three_d.fallback_mobile: Particles still run at 390px (mobile_00/01) with the same fixed composition; product browsing moves into a swipe row of cards.

performance_accessibility.weight_notes: Light for a 3D site: ~5.8MB declared total; 3D 1.03MB, JS ~1.03MB, images ~2.7MB.
performance_accessibility.reduced_motion: probe reduced_motion_rules 0 in CSS; the JS reads matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') once, sets blur-in text to its final state and skips two SVG line animations; the particle field, the plate timers and the exploded spin have no reduced path.
performance_accessibility.contrast_issues: Brand manifesto lives only in canvas particles (haiku are JPG-sampled positions), blurred and partly unreadable (desktop_01, mobile_01) and invisible to assistive tech; the headline tail is #DDDEE3 at opacity .5 on #101010 and the 11.2px labels on #101010 are low contrast; SplitText runs with aria:'none', so split headings get no aria-label and may be read character by character. steal_this.technique: GPGPU particles that settle on Chladni nodal lines and into words
steal_this.why_it_works: Physics of sound made visible is the product story; the pattern is generative, so every visit and every cursor pass looks different.
steal_this.how_to_build: Two ping-pong float RGBA render targets (here 1280x1280 = 1.64M particles; start at 512x512 on weaker GPUs) storing xy position + xy velocity. Text targets: draw each word JPG (dark text on light) to a 400*dpr canvas, collect pixels with red < 120, give every particle a random one as a vec2 target in a float DataTexture (u_original). Sim fragment: pick = hash21(uv) < u_texturePercent ? 1. : 0.; pattern target = the particle's grid position pulled onto nodal lines (Chladni f = sin(m*PI*x/2.)*sin(n*PI*y/2.) on plate coords 0..2, numeric gradient eps 0.01, one Newton step pos += normalize(g)*(-f/length(g))*0.3*distortion, attraction 0.45, line push 0.12, tangential shimmer 0.05 along the line); target = mix(patternTarget, textTarget, pick); vel *= pow(0.985, dt*60); vel += dir(target)*0.0005*(pick>0.5 ? 5. : 1.)*dt60 (pattern particles stop within 0.01 of the line); vel += randomDir*0.00035*(pick>0.5 ? 0.1 : 0.3)*dt60; vel += radial push from the pointer * (1-smoothstep(0,1,dist/0.16)) * 0.0225 * smoothedPointerSpeed * dt60; pos += vel*dt60. Render THREE.Points at 1px, white at low alpha on #101010. Drive it with timers, not input: m,n from [3,5,7] every 6-12s, frequency 20-45 every 5-10s, noise and distortion tweened on 2-5s / 1.2-3s power2.inOut loops, and per frame add +/-0.5 random jitter to m,n before the shader rounds them. Haiku loop: texturePercent -> 0 over 0.4N (N = 3-6s), swap u_original, -> 0.4-0.8 over 0.6N, hold 2-4s, repeat. Seed the initial positions on the first text so the first frame is already a word-shaped cloud.

steal_this.technique: A self-retuning instrument instead of a scroll story
steal_this.why_it_works: The page never moves, so the corner-anchored headline, nav and shop tile stay composed, while the canvas keeps changing on its own like a plate being played; the visitor's only role is to disturb it with the pointer. (The first-pass 'wheel as a state machine' reading was wrong: the bundle has no wheel handler on the home canvas.)
steal_this.how_to_build: Keep document height = 100vh and give the canvas several independent gsap.delayedCall loops with randomised periods (6-12s modes, 5-10s frequency, 4-8s jitter) plus tweened loops for continuous values (noise 2-5s, distortion 1.2-3s, power2.inOut), so the state rarely repeats and the changes overlap instead of stepping in sync. Set discrete values instantly (the particle physics smooths them) and tween continuous ones. Keep text in a separate, slower loop (7-13s per haiku) so words and pattern drift in and out of phase. Kill every loop on page leave.

steal_this.why_it_works: Spec sheet becomes exploration; the clear shell with visible internals makes 'computer inside an earbud' believable.
steal_this.how_to_build: GLB with parts as separate meshes; offset each along the device axis: z = [0.6, 0.15, -0.6][i] * explodeProgress. ScrollTrigger({trigger: section, start:'top 50%', end:'bottom 50%', toggleActions:'play reverse play reverse'}) on a timeline: set {ry: PI/2, z: 0.3, explodeProgress: 0}; to {ry: -PI/2, z: 0} 1s expo.inOut ('spin'); to {explodeProgress: 1} 1.8s CustomEase('M0,0 C0,1.175 0.3,1.021 1,1') at 'spin+=0.5'. Each frame: group.rotation.x = pointerY*0.2 + ctrl.rx, rotation.y = pointerX*0.2 + ctrl.ry, plus an idle loop tweening y/rx/rz by +/-0.05-0.09 over 3-5s sine.inOut. Raycast on pointermove only when explodeProgress >= 0.4: hovered part scale 1.085-1.3 and rotate to a per-part showcase angle, others scale 0.8, 2.5s expo.out. DOM card with its top-left at the pointer: dark glass (rgba(33,33,33,.69) + blur), thumbnail, ~14px title, ~11px 3-4 line grey description (card crossfade timing inferred). Clear core: MeshPhysicalMaterial {transmission:1, roughness:0.05, thickness:0.018, ior:1.6}; silicone tip {transmission:0.62, thickness:0.2, attenuationDistance:0.1, roughness:0.53, ior:1.42, color:#C7C7C7}; EXR environment.

steal_this.technique: View-dependent matcap colourways with a ripple wipe
steal_this.why_it_works: A matcap computed from the view vector gives the face an iridescent shift as it turns (periwinkle face-on, yellow-pink-lilac tilted) for the price of one small image per finish, and switching finishes as a ripple spreading across the face ties the configurator back to the site's sound/cymatics idea.
steal_this.how_to_build: Patch the product's PBR material with onBeforeCompile. Vertex: vView = normalize(-(modelViewMatrix*vec4(position,1.)).xyz); vN = normalize((modelViewMatrix*vec4(normal,0.)).xyz). Fragment (after dithering_fragment): vec3 x = normalize(vec3(vView.z, 0., -vView.x)); vec3 y = cross(vView, x); vec2 muv = vec2(dot(x, vN), dot(y, vN))*0.495 + 0.5 (view-corrected matcap, the bundle's exact lines; the ripple below runs on the mesh's own vUv, not on the matcap UV); colour = mix(pbrColor, matcap, 0.82). Keep three matcaps (dusk/night/dawn webp) and a target index. Swatch click: tween uTransitionProgress 0 -> 1 over 1.2s power2.out; in the shader d = length(vUv - 0.5); eased = 1 - pow(1 - p, 2.5); radius = eased*0.707*1.2; wobble d with three sines of d*8 - p*8 (amps 0.15, 0.08, 0.04, x0.3) plus small uv noise; mask = 1 - smoothstep(radius - w, radius + w, d) with w = 0.15 + 0.1p; blend current -> target matcap by mask; on complete set current = target. Swap metal colours per finish on the same click. Dock options in a fixed glass panel (26rem, radius 2rem, blur 20px, #38383899 + a 141deg #a9c2f214 -> #62718c24 tint) with accordion rows opened by grid-template-rows 0fr -> 1fr.

steal_this.technique: Blur-in and scrub-fill text with a reduced-motion exit
steal_this.why_it_works: Copy arrives like focus pulling, echoing the grain on the canvas, and still degrades to static text.
steal_this.how_to_build: GSAP SplitText {type:'words,chars'} (use the default aria mode, not aria:'none' as the site does). Blur-in: set chars {autoAlpha:0, filter:'blur(2px)'} from JS (so no-JS shows text), then on IntersectionObserver entry gsap.to(chars,{autoAlpha:1, filter:'blur(0px)', duration:1.1, ease:'linear', stagger:{each:0.02, from:0}}); on exit kill and reset so it replays. Scrub fill: SplitText {type:'words, chars', autoSplit:true, onSplit} -> timeline with scrollTrigger {trigger, start:'top 90%', end:'center 40%', scrub:true} .fromTo(chars,{autoAlpha:0.2},{autoAlpha:1, stagger:0.1, ease:'linear'}). If matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') set final values and skip.

steal_this.technique: Capsule nav that grows into the menu
steal_this.why_it_works: One glass object carries the wordmark, menu and cart, and opening it reads as the same object changing shape rather than a new panel arriving.
steal_this.how_to_build: Fixed capsule 23.5rem wide, top 2rem, centred, border-radius 3em, glass = backdrop-filter blur(20px) + background #38383899 + linear-gradient(141deg, #a9c2f214, #62718c24). Inside, a content row with display:grid; grid-template-rows:0fr and an inner wrapper with overflow:hidden. Open state (data-navigation-status=active): grid-template-rows:1fr over 0.6s cubic-bezier(.625,.05,0,1) with a 0.125s delay, border-radius 2em immediately; closed state delays the radius change 0.45s so the corners round only after the panel has folded. Menu cards: on hover set siblings to opacity 0.2 (0.15s) and scale the hovered image 1.04 over 0.4s cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,.94). Close on Escape and outside click.

slop_risks: Botched glass: the capsule nav and panels are blur(20px) over #38383899 with a 141deg cool-tint gradient, but on home they sit on a near-black particle field with little to refract, so the blur reads as a flat grey capsule; on the pale configurator it works better. A copy over a plain dark fill is the botched-glass tell.

One label treatment everywhere: SHOP NOW, DETAILS, YOUR CONFIGURATION, CONNECTIVITY, PICK UP A COLOR and OTHER PRODUCTS all wear the same 11.2px tracked uppercase mono. The eyebrow face (NB Architekt) looks near-monospaced in captures, so this also edges toward mono as the house voice for every label.
Grain over text: the haiku is grain by design and often unreadable (desktop_01, mobile_01); fine as one deliberate display element, slop if copied as a noise sheet over body copy.

Radial glow halo, partly a false accusation: the bright central ellipse in desktop_00/07 is not a glow blob but particles gathered on the haiku's letter positions (desktop_00 = the seeded start, desktop_07 = the next haiku condensing). The risk is real only for a copy: without legible words forming out of it, a soft centred particle cloud behind nothing reads as the halo tell.
Fixed background that trails the scroll: a full-screen fixed particle canvas copied without the state changes and cursor physics is exactly this tell.
Purple/blue gradient: the Dusk finish is a lilac-blue to pink gradient disc; it is the real product colour here, but lifting it as a UI gradient is the blue-purple tell.

Filled-button-next-to-outlined-button pair: the mobile product cards pair an outlined LEARN MORE pill with a filled light SHOP NOW pill (mobile_00/01), the stock fill-versus-outline couplet; pick one action per card or differentiate them another way.
Default CTA pair: 'Pre Order Now' dark pill plus a detached round arrow button (element 3) sits close to the pill-plus-arrow preset.
Content that exists only in the canvas: the manifesto haiku are JPG textures, invisible to screen readers and search.
confidence_notes: OBSERVED: all 8 desktop screenshots and both mobiles (home only; the document is a single 900px viewport, so all 8 steps show state changes rather than new sections); all 8 frames of element 0 (Chladni haiku) and element 2 (exploded view); f00/f03/f06 of element 1 (configurator) and element 3 (footer shader). Code: 3 fetches (Webflow HTML, iyo2.vercel.app/app.js, app.css) with tight greps; the particle uniforms, their defaults and the Chladni GLSL are quoted from the bundle. INFERRED: particle count, the exact wheel-to-scene quantisation, which Lenis options belong to Lenis rather than other lerps, foundry of Magnetik, the configurator background hex, sound behaviour (uniforms exist, no audio code found). Menu/cart and 404 elements were not in the frame set. audit 2 (2026-09-25, adversarial pass; re-viewed desktop_00-07, mobile_00/01, element 0 f00-f07, element 2 f00/f02/f04/f06/f07, element 1 f00-f03/f06, element 3 f00/f03/f06 one at a time; re-fetched the live HTML, iyo2.vercel.app/app.js, app.css and the Webflow shared CSS): FIXED (1) the signature and steal #2 claimed wheel ticks change the Chladni mode; the bundle drives modes, frequency, jitter, noise, distortion and the haiku cycle with randomized gsap timers, the probe's wheel steps only passed time (same haiku in desktop_01-04), and steal #2 was replaced; (2) infinite:true is the product slider's virtual-scroll config, Lenis is {lerp .125, infinite false}; (3) particle count 1280x1280 = 1.64M (not the guessed 512x512), text targets are CPU-sampled dark pixels (red < 120) of the JPGs, not a white-on-black mask read in the sim; (4) the mouse is a radial push scaled by pointer speed, not a swirl; home strength/radius 0.0225/0.16; text particles pull 5x harder; (5) the exploded view is a scroll-triggered 180-degree spin + 1.8s overshoot explode with a small pointer tilt, not pointer-following; hover scales parts 1.085-1.3 / others 0.8 over 2.5s; material values in the steal were invented (thickness 0.5, clearcoat 1) and are replaced by the bundle's presets; (6) configurator recolour is a 1.2s ripple wipe between view-dependent matcaps, not instant; panel is 26rem not 250px; bg is #DDDEE3; (7) page transitions are Taxi.js PJAX fades (0.15s out / 0.2s in) with a body-colour swap, not separate page loads; (8) headline tail is opacity .5, not a separate grey; webgl2 contexts are 2, not 1; GSAP ease counts recounted; the 'radial glow halo' accusation was mostly false. ADDED: configurator ring + trailing ball cursor with drag chevrons, grid-rows capsule-to-menu morph (new steal), mobile card auto-advance (5s), 404 line speeds, silent-site verification (no audio code), filled+outlined button pair slop risk, SplitText aria:'none'. STILL INFERRED: Magnetik foundry, whether NB Architekt is monospaced, the spec-card crossfade timing, the footer card collapse trigger, the finish-to-metal-colour index mapping.
